subject: Copywriting
title: Tiffany & Co.: The Color Is the Copy
description: A quick, practical guide to Tiffany & Co.: The Color Is the Copy.

buildup.text: Tiffany's copy is warm and intimate: 'Some things never change' and 'True love.' The tone is a love letter, not an ad.

discovery.text: The 1961 film 'Breakfast at Tiffany's' gave the brand literary glamour.

twist.text: After LVMH acquired Tiffany in 2021, the copy pivoted: 'Not Your Mother's Tiffany.' Heritage gave way to rebellion.

climax.text: Tiffany proves a color can be copy. When the visual identity is strong enough, words are accessories, not essentials.

punchline.text: Pantone 1837. A color so powerful it doesn't need words to sell.

quiz.question: What is the Pantone number of Tiffany blue?

details.summary: Tiffany's robin's-egg blue box is the most recognized luxury packaging in the world. The brand needs barely any copy because the color itself communicates everything: romance, elegance, and anticipation. details.whyItMatters: Tiffany proves that when visual identity is strong enough, copy becomes supplementary. The brand teaches writers that communications extend beyond words — color, packaging, and experience are all forms of copy.
takeaways: Tiffany Blue is the most recognized luxury color in the world
The blue box communicates romance and elegance without any words
Visual identity can be so powerful it replaces the need for copy

faq.question: How did Tiffany Blue become so iconic?
faq.answer: Consistency since 1837. Every Tiffany product arrives in the same shade of blue, creating a Pavlovian association between the color and the feeling of receiving luxury. The color is trademarked and never used for anything except Tiffany packaging, maintaining its exclusivity.

faq.question: What does Tiffany teach about luxury brand communication?
faq.answer: That communication extends beyond words. Color, packaging, the weight of a box, the sound of a clasp — all communicate brand values. Great luxury 'copywriting' considers every sensory touchpoint, not just the words on the page.
